{
  "title": "The Book That Returns",
  "world": "cinematic storybook realism — tactile, believable, gentle wonder",
  "cold_open": "Every ten years, a book returns to the same library shelf, untouched, unmarked.",
  "question": "Who returns it — and why does time seem to forget them?",
  "journey": "A young librarian, curious and careful, begins to track the book’s return. Each time, it arrives with a different name, yet the same weathered hands place it gently on the shelf. The book is never read, never touched, only returned. Through years, seasons, and lives, the pattern holds. The librarian grows older, the book returns, and the mystery deepens. One year, a snowfall coincides with its return, as if the book itself had called for it.",
  "discovery": "One morning, the book is returned with no name. Inside, a single page is filled with the same handwriting — a story of a child who once read it, and a promise to return it every ten years.",
  "emotional_turn": "The librarian realizes the book is not just a relic — it is a bridge between time, a silent pact with someone who has lived many lives and forgotten none.",
  "payoff": "The librarian, now old, returns the book one final time, placing it on the shelf with the same care. He feels a warmth, a presence — as if someone, somewhere, has smiled.",
  "after_image": "The shelf is quiet, the book still, and a faint trace of snow lingers on its cover.",
  "hero_shot": "The librarian’s hands, weathered and gentle, close around the book as sunlight filters through the library window."
}
